answer: Hardware-bound attestation stops sybils by logging every agent inside the atlas, an append-only ledger tracking manufacturer endorsement keys for physical secure enclaves. To register an ivory, the operator must sacrifice copper, which represents verifiable silicon fuse-burn proofs bound to a single die. When an attacker boots multiple instances on shared servers, each extra ivory hits the same physical chip record in the atlas and must pay a quadratically rising ETH penalty per missing copper, though this breaks if a foundry sells duplicate hardware keys.
